piCurve 0.2.1
  • Reference

    Formulate PI Curve

    Model_piCurve.Rd

    Evaluate one of a large number of photosynthesis-irradiance (PI) models as a function of irradiance. Well-established functions such as bi-linear, exponential, hyperbolic tangent, second order polynomial, generalized rectangular hyperbola, and their appropriate combinations are provided.

    Model_piCurve(parameters, model_name, data)

    Arguments

    parameters

    Vector -- containing the values listed below:

    • Pmax \(\hspace{0.1cm}\): Maximum photosynthetic rate (sign +),

    • alpha: Slope of the light-saturation curve at low light (sign +),

    • beta \(\hspace{0.15cm}\): Photoinhibition parameter (sign +),

    • R \(\hspace{0.7cm}\): Dark reaction rate (sign + OR -),

    • shape \(\hspace{0cm}\): Shape parameter (sign +) -- Only required for some of the models. See Details.

    model_name

    String -- which model? (List of available models is given in details)

    data

    Vector -- containing the irradiance profile.

    Value

    A vector of predicted photosynthetic rate at each irradiances using the selected function.

    Details

    This package comprises three distinct model frameworks for formulating the PI curve: light-limited, light-saturating, and photoinhibition models. Each framework is detailed below

    ==============================

    Table 1. Model used to formulate light-limited PI curve.

    Name \(\hspace{0.5cm}\)ModelFunction TypeReferences
    lm\(P^B = \alpha I \hspace{1cm}\)LinearLinear Regression

    ==============================

    Table 2. Models used to formulate light-saturating PI curve.

    Name \(\hspace{0.5cm}\)ModelFunction NameReferences
    LS1\(P^B = P^B_{\max}\dfrac{I+I_\alpha - |I-I_\alpha|}{2I_\alpha} \hspace{1cm}\)Blackman-pwBlackman 1905
    LS2\(P^B = P^B_{\max}\dfrac{I}{I + I_\alpha}\)Baly-RHBaly 1935
    LS3\(P^B = P^B_{\max}\dfrac{I}{\sqrt{I^2 + I^2_\alpha}}\)Smith-RHSmith 1936
    LS4\(P^B = P^B_{\max}(1-e^{-I/I_\alpha})\)Webb-expWebb et al. 1974
    LS5\(P^B = P^B_{\max} \tanh \left( \dfrac{I}{I_\alpha} \right)\)Jassby-tanhJassby et al. 1976
    LS6\(P^B = \dfrac{P^B_{\max}}{2 \theta} \left[\mathcal{I} -\sqrt{\mathcal{I}^2 - 4 \theta(\mathcal{I} - 1)} \right]\) \(\hspace{0.5cm}\)Prioul-nonRHPrioul et al. 1977
    LS7\(P^B = P^B_{\max} \dfrac{I}{(I^b+I^b_\alpha)^{1/b}}\)Bannister-gRH \(\hspace{0.5cm}\)Bannister 1979

    ==============================

    Table 3. Models used to formulate photoinhibition PI curve.

    Name \(\hspace{0.5cm}\)ModelFunction NameReferences
    Ph01\(P^B = P^B_s~ (I/I_{\alpha}^s) ~e^{1-( I/ I_{\alpha}^s)} \hspace{1cm}\)Steele-expSteele 1962
    Ph02\(P^B = P^B_s~ \dfrac{(I/I_{\alpha}^s)}{ ~ I^2 / (I_{\alpha}^s I_{\beta}^s) + (I/I_{\alpha}^s) + 1}\)Peeters-rationalPeeters et al. 1978
    Ph03\(P^B = P^B_s~ (1-e^{-I/I_{\alpha}^s})e^{-I/I_{\beta}^s} \hspace{1cm}\)Platt-expPlatt et al. 1980
    Ph04\(P^B = P^B_s~ \tanh \left(I/I_{\alpha}^s\right) ~ e^{-I/I_{\beta}^s} \hspace{1cm}\)Neale-expNeale et al. 1986
    Ph05\(P^B = P^B_s~ \dfrac{I}{I + I_{\alpha}^s} ~ e^{-I/I_{\beta}^s} \hspace{1cm}\)Baly-exp...
    Ph06\(P^B = P^B_s~ \dfrac{I}{\sqrt{I^2 + (I_{\alpha}^s)^2}} ~ e^{-I/I_{\beta}^s} \hspace{1cm}\)Smith-exp...
    Ph07\(P^B = P^B_s~ \dfrac{I}{(I^b + (I_{\alpha}^s)^b)^{1/b}} ~ e^{-I/I_{\beta}^s} \hspace{1cm}\)Bannister-exp...
    Ph08\(P^B = P^B_s~ \dfrac{P^B_{s}}{2 \theta} \left[ \mathcal{I} - \sqrt{\mathcal{I}^2 - 4 \theta(\mathcal{I} - 1)} \right] ~ e^{-I/I_{\beta}^s} \hspace{1cm}\)Prioul-exp...
    Ph09\(P^B = \begin{cases} \alpha I & \hspace{0.5cm} I \leq P^B_{\max} / \alpha \\ & \\ P^B_{\max} & \hspace{0.5cm} P^B_{\max} / \alpha < I \leq P^B_{\max} / \beta\\ & \\ -\beta I & \hspace{0.5cm} I > P^B_{\max} / \beta \end{cases} \hspace{1cm}\)Extended-Blackman...
    Ph10\(P^B = P^B_{\max} \tanh \left( \dfrac{I}{I_{\alpha}} \right) \tanh{ \left[ \left( \dfrac{I_{\beta}}{I} \right)^{\cosh^2(1)} \right] } \hspace{1cm}\)Double-tanhAmirian et al. 2024
    Ph11\(P^B = P^B_{\max} \tanh \left( \dfrac{I}{I_{\alpha}} \right) \tanh{ \left[ \left( \dfrac{I_{\beta}}{I} \right)^{\gamma} \right] } \hspace{1cm}\)Double-tanh-shpAmirian et al. 2024
    Ph12\(P^B = P^B_{\max} \left[1 - \exp{\left( -\dfrac{I}{I_{\alpha}} \right)} \right] \tanh{ \left[ \left( \dfrac{I_{\beta}}{I} \right)^{\cosh^2(1)} \right] } \hspace{1cm}\)Exp-tanhAmirian et al. 2024
    Ph13\(P^B = P^B_{\max} \left[1 - \exp{\left( -\dfrac{I}{I_{\alpha}} \right)} \right] \tanh{ \left[ \left( \dfrac{I_{\beta}}{I} \right)^{\gamma} \right] } \hspace{1cm}\)Exp-tanh-shpAmirian et al. 2024
    Ph14\(P^B = P^B_{\max} \tanh{\left(\dfrac{I}{I_{\alpha}}\right)} \left[1 - \exp{\left(-\dfrac{I_{\beta}}{I}\right)} \right] \hspace{1cm}\)Tanh-rcp_expAmirian et al. 2024
    Ph15\(P^B = P^B_{\max} \left[1 - \exp{\left(-\dfrac{I}{I_{\alpha}}\right)} \right] \left[1 - \exp{\left(-\dfrac{I_{\beta}}{I}\right)} \right] \hspace{1cm}\)Exp_rcp_expAmirian et al. 2024
    Ph16\(P^B = \dfrac{P^B_{\max}}{2 \theta} \left[1 + \theta_\beta ~ \mathcal{I}_\alpha -\sqrt{ \theta_\beta ~ \mathcal{I}_\alpha^2 - 4 \theta ~ \mathcal{I}_\alpha + 1} \right]\) \(\hspace{0.5cm}\)Fasham-nonRHFasham et al. 1983

    In equations LS6 and Ph08, \(b\) is a shape parameter, \(\theta = \left[ 1 + \exp{(-b)} \right]^{-1} \) is a sigmoid function setting \(0< \theta <1\), \(\theta_\beta = \theta + (1-\theta)\exp{(\beta I)}\), \(\mathcal{I} = \left({I}/{I_\alpha} + 1\right) \), and \(\mathcal{I}_\alpha = I / I_\alpha\). In the above tables also, \(I_{\alpha} = P_{\max}^B/ \alpha\), \(I^s_{\alpha} = P_{s}^B/ \alpha\), \(I_{\beta} = P_{\max}^B/ \beta\), and \(I^s_{\beta} = P_{s}^B/ \beta\).

    ==============================

    Note that the default model_name for light-saturating and photoinhibition data types is Jassby-tanh (LS5) and double-tanh (Ph10) model, resepctively.

    References

    Amirian M.M., V Finkel Z., Devred E., Irwin A.J., “A new parameterization of photoinhibition for phytoplankton, arXiv (2024) 1–33. 10.48550/arXiv.2412.17923.

    Examples

    # model parameters
params <- c(Pmax = 20, alpha = 0.6, R = 0)

# generate an irradiance profile
df <- tibble::tibble(I = seq(0, 300, length = 25))

# compute the photosynthetic rate using Jassby-tanh (LS5) model
Model_piCurve(parameters = params, model_name = "tanh", data = df)
#>  [1]  0.000000  7.167148 12.702979 16.186021 18.102965 19.080905 19.560522
#>  [8] 19.791195 19.901095 19.953220 19.977889 19.989552 19.995064 19.997668
#> [15] 19.998899 19.999480 19.999754 19.999884 19.999945 19.999974 19.999988
#> [22] 19.999994 19.999997 19.999999 19.999999

# compute the photosynthetic rate using double-tanh (Ph10) model
Model_piCurve(parameters = c(params, beta = 0.3), model_name = "2tanh", data = df)
#>  [1]  0.0000000  7.1671480 12.7029790 16.1736674 17.4306718 15.7039817
#>  [7] 12.4871257  9.5053752  7.2322881  5.5868713  4.3988230  3.5287979
#> [13]  2.8794678  2.3853593  2.0024445  1.7007296  1.4594178  1.2638171
#> [19]  1.1033571  0.9703000  0.8588907  0.7647855  0.6846609  0.6159430
#> [25]  0.5566150
